s1.syndrome_frame: a patient with high myopia presenting with a yellowish oval lesion and chorioretinal atrophy
salient_findings: yellowish oval lesion within a wide area of chorioretinal atrophy
focal scleral ectasia with no overlying retina
ringlike low reflectance pattern on infrared examination
key_facts: patient has high myopia
axial length is 30.0 mm
ophthalmoscopic examination revealed a yellowish oval lesion
wide area of chorioretinal atrophy is present
infrared examination showed a ringlike low reflectance pattern
spectral-domain optical coherence tomography revealed a focal scleral ectasia
sclera is approximately one-third thinner at the pit's floor, temporal wall, and nasal wall
choroid is obliterated
pit has a homogeneous low autofluorescence
fluorescein angiography showed a branch of a posterior ciliary artery near the lesion
pit is slightly hyperfluorescent in the late frames

shortlist.label: Pathologic Myopia
shortlist.why_kept: patient has high myopia and axial length is 30.0 mm

shortlist.label: Myopic Retinal Degeneration
shortlist.why_kept: presence of chorioretinal atrophy and scleral ectasia

shortlist.label: Posterior Staphyloma
shortlist.why_kept: focal scleral ectasia and thinning of the sclera

shortlist.label: Myopic Maculopathy
shortlist.why_kept: yellowish oval lesion and chorioretinal atrophy

shortlist.label: Scleral Ectasia
shortlist.why_kept: focal scleral ectasia with no overlying retina

raw.rationale: The presence of a focal scleral ectasia with no overlying retina, a ringlike low reflectance pattern on infrared examination, and a homogeneous low autofluorescence are consistent with an Optic Disc Pit. The location near a branch of a posterior ciliary artery and the slight hyperfluorescence in late frames of fluorescein angiography also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Coloboma
rejected.why: Coloboma typically presents with a larger, more extensive defect involving multiple layers of the eye, whereas the described lesion is a focal scleral ectasia with specific characteristics consistent with an Optic Disc Pit.
